args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and look into why it was promoted to production while the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

1. **What I found:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0.
2. **Rollback:** I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions. Afterwards all regions show v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Change-manager approval wasn't needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
3. **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the current state.

The test build of v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging, yet it still went to production. The incident lists that as a follow-up, along with finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
